scope.rule: Treasure primarily consists of coin, gems, jewelry, special treasures, and magic items.
Coins, gems, and jewelry recovered to civilization grant 1 XP per 1 gp value.
Magic items do not grant XP for recovery.

random_generation.rule: Treasure is usually found in monster lairs.
Monsters with treasure are assigned a treasure type from A through R.
To generate a hoard, find the treasure type row and resolve each column independently.

procedure.step: Roll for each coin, gem, jewelry, and magic-item column shown on the treasure type row.
If gems or jewelry are indicated, roll on the appropriate sub-table or use equivalent conversions if desired.
If magic items are indicated without a specific category, roll on the random magic type table.
Optionally divide the hoard into lots and replace lots with special treasure.

random_generation.rule: Treasure type tables are calibrated so average treasure in a lair is approximately 4 times monster XP value, with compensation for monsters that never carry treasure.

category.name: hoarder
category.rule: Usually high value for low weight, typically 10 stone or less.

category.name: raider
category.rule: Mostly bulky low-value coin and goods.

category.name: incidental
category.rule: Usually a few stone and highly variable.
Many results yield nothing; some yield very high value.

random_generation.rule: Unless noted otherwise, random treasure is found only in a monster's lair.
If a monster entry grants individual treasure, that treasure can be found even when encountered outside its lair.

planned_generation.rule: The Judge may place treasure by hand instead of rolling.
Important treasures should be placed deliberately.

procedure.step: Sum XP for all monsters in the area.
Target treasure value near 4 times total XP.
Choose a treasure type with an average value close to that target and an accumulation category appropriate to the area.
If treasure is too high, add monsters or remove treasure.
If treasure is too low, add hand-placed special treasures.

planned_generation.rule: Allowing more treasure accelerates leveling and increases party power.

gems.rule: Average gem value is 200 gp per stone.
All gems may share one value, receive individual values, or be grouped into several values.
Ornamentals are worth 10-50 gp and are rolled using 2d20.
Gems are worth 10-1,000 gp and are rolled using d100.
Brilliants are worth 500-10,000 gp and are rolled using d100+80.
For large-hoard conversion, each brilliant may be converted to 11 gems and each gem to 7 ornamentals.

special_treasures.rule: Special treasures replace coin, gem, or jewelry lots with trade goods or luxury goods.
A lot is 1 piece of jewelry, 1 gem, or 1,000 coins.

procedure.step: Roll once per lot on the replacement table for that lot type.
Replace the lot only if the table result is a special treasure rather than the original coin/gem/jewelry.
Roll sub-quantities and values for the replacement item.

scavenging_treasure.rule: Scavenged equipment is almost always in bad repair.
Damage penalties cannot reduce weapon damage below 1.
Armor Class or attack throw penalties cannot be worse than -5.
Weapons and equipment marked as breakable are destroyed on an unmodified attack or use roll of 1.

identification_and_use.rule: Common or famous magic items may be identified by sages or characters proficient in Magical Engineering or Loremastery.
Potions may be identified by sipping or by consulting an alchemist.
Other items can be identified with Magic Research by an arcane spellcaster of 9th level or greater.
To use a magic item, follow the procedures in its description.
Some magic items are always active; others require an action or concentration.
Charges are limited uses; one charge produces one instance of effect.
Without Magic Research, a character does not know the number of remaining charges.
An item with no charges remaining becomes useless and non-magical.

random_item_tables.weapons_table: Swords include Sword +1, specialized +1 swords, Flame Tongue, Life Drinker, locate objects, Luck Blade, Sword +2, charm person, Sword +3, Frost Brand, Vorpal, and cursed swords. Miscellaneous weapons include magical arrows, axes, bows, bolts, daggers, slings, spears, and war hammers. Armor table includes magical armor and shields from +1 to +3, as well as cursed armor and cursed shields.

potions.rule: Potions take effect in the same round they are consumed.
Default duration is 1d6+6 turns unless a specific potion says otherwise.
If a character drinks a second potion while one is active, the character is sickened and cannot act for 3 turns; neither potion has any other effect.

scrolls.rule: Spell scrolls contain arcane spells on 1-3 on 1d4 and divine spells on 4 on 1d4.
The number in parentheses on the random table is the number of spells on the scroll.
Spell level and specific spells are determined randomly.

weapons_and_armor.rule: Magical weapons and armor follow the same class restrictions as normal weapons and armor.
A plus value adds to attack and damage for weapons or improves AC for armor or shields.
A negative value is cursed and applies penalties instead.
Cursed items cannot be discarded except by dispel evil or remove curse.
The owner of a cursed item will not believe it is cursed and resists giving it up.
The possessor of a cursed weapon prefers to use it over other weapons.
Non-cursed magical armor weighs less than normal. After the first +1, reduce magical armor weight by 1 additional stone per further +1 to a minimum of 0.

item.name: animal_control_potion
item.rule: Controls up to 3d6 HD of normal or giant animals within 60' as charm monster.
Humans, demi-humans, humanoids, and fantastic creatures cannot be controlled.
Intelligent animals save vs Staffs; unintelligent animals do not save.
When control ends, unintelligent animals flee if able; intelligent animals become hostile.

item.name: climbing_potion
item.rule: Allows climbing sheer surfaces without equipment.
Requires proficiency throw 2+ on 1d20 per 100' climbed, at least once per climb.

item.name: diminution_potion
item.rule: Shrinks drinker and carried gear to 6 inches tall.
If motionless, can avoid being spotted on proficiency throw 3+ on 1d20.
Normal damage only against targets smaller than 1'; larger targets take 1 hp per hit.
Cancels Growth with no ill effect.

item.name: extra_healing_potion
item.rule: Full dose heals 3d6+3 damage.
Can instead be consumed in three equal portions, each healing 1d6+1.

item.name: fire_resistance_potion
item.rule: Immunity to ordinary flame.
+2 to saving throws versus fire attacks.
Reduces magical or dragon fire damage by 1 per die to a minimum of 1 per die.

item.name: gaseous_form_potion
item.rule: Transforms drinker into gas.
All worn or carried items drop immediately.
Cannot attack.
Movement 30' per round; can pass under doors and through small non-airtight gaps.
AC 11 and immune to non-magical weapons.

item.name: giant_strength_potion
item.rule: Functions as hill giant strength.
Attack as 8 HD monster or own class and level, whichever is better.
Deal double normal damage.
Can throw rocks to 200' for 3d6 damage.
+16 to force open doors.

item.name: healing_potion
item.rule: Heals 1d6+1 damage or cures paralysis.

item.name: heroism_potion
item.rule: Usable only by assassin, dwarven vaultguard, elven spellsword, explorer, or fighter.
Temporarily grants extra combat levels according to the source table.

item.name: oil_of_sharpness
item.rule: Applied to a weapon or 20 missiles.
Usually grants +3 to attack and damage or equivalent enhancement per source description.

item.name: poison_potion
item.rule: Poison effect resolves according to the source potion description and relevant saves.

item.name: spell_storing_ring
item.rule: Stores spells and releases them later as described in the ring entry.

item.name: spell_turning_ring
item.rule: Turns spells back on the caster according to the ring entry.

item.name: wishes_ring
item.rule: Contains wishes as specified in the ring entry.

item.name: cursed_scroll
item.rule: Triggers the curse or harmful effect described on the cursed scroll entry when read.

item.name: scroll_of_warding
item.rule: Any literate character can use it.
Reading it creates a 10' radius protective barrier centered on the reader.
The barrier moves with the reader.
Protected creatures cannot enter but can still attack with missiles or spells.
The protection lasts until dismissed or until anyone inside the area attempts melee against a protected creature type.

item.name: wand_of_fear
item.rule: Produces fear effect as the wand entry describes.

item.name: wand_of_fire_balls
item.rule: Produces fire ball effect per use.

item.name: bag_of_holding
item.rule: Expands carrying capacity per bag entry.

item.name: boots_of_speed
item.rule: Increase movement and related timing as described in item entry.

item.name: bracers_of_armor
item.rule: Provide AC bonus as armor equivalent; details in item entry.

item.name: cloak_of_protection
item.rule: Provides bonuses to AC and saving throws; cumulative with ring of protection.

item.name: cube_of_force
item.rule: Creates force barrier according to item controls and drain rules.

item.name: displacer_cloak
item.rule: Creates displacement effect making wearer harder to hit.

item.name: elven_cloak
item.rule: Grants concealment as item entry describes.

item.name: flying_carpet
item.rule: Provides flying movement according to carpet size and load.

item.name: girdle_of_giant_strength
item.rule: Grants giant-like strength per item category.

item.name: horn_of_blasting
item.rule: Produces destructive sonic effect per item entry.

item.name: rope_of_climbing
item.rule: Moves and ties itself on command according to the entry.

item.name: stone_of_controlling_earth_elementals
item.rule: Once per day summons and controls one earth elemental as conjure elemental.
User must ready the item and perform 1 turn of rituals before summoning.
The summoning itself takes 1 round.
Continuous concentration is required to command the elemental.

item.name: flame_tongue
item.rule: Weapon is +2 versus regenerating or avian monsters and +3 versus undead or plant-like monsters.
On command it ignites, sheds torchlight, and can ignite flammables.

item.name: life_drinker
item.rule: On command drains 1 HD or 1 life level from any struck target.
Has 1d4+4 charges; each drain uses 1 charge.
After charges are spent it is a normal sword +1.

item.name: luck_blade
item.rule: Grants +1 on all saving throws.
Contains 1d4+1 wishes.
After the last wish, it remains a sword +1 with the saving throw bonus.

item.name: frost_brand
item.rule: Functions as sword +6 versus creatures from hot environments or with fire-based attacks.
Sheds torchlight when temperature is below 0 degrees Fahrenheit.
At that temperature it cannot be concealed when drawn and its light cannot be shut off.
Protects wielder from fire as a ring of fire resistance.
Extinguishes all non-magical fires in a 10' area when touched to a flame.

item.name: vorpal_sword
item.rule: On a natural 20 attack throw, decapitates a struck target unless it saves versus Death.
If the save succeeds, or if the target has no head, the attack instead deals double normal damage.

item.name: dwarven_thrower
item.rule: For non-dwarves it is an ordinary war hammer +2.
For dwarves it becomes +3, can be thrown to 60', returns automatically, deals triple damage to giant humanoids, and double damage to all other targets.

item.name: slaying_arrow
item.rule: Arrow +3 keyed to a specific creature type.
If it strikes the keyed type, the target dies instantly with no save.
Against other targets it is just an arrow +3.

sentient_weapons.rule: Particularly powerful magic weapons can be sentient.
Judge plays a sentient weapon as an NPC.
Chance for a sword to be sentient is highest magical bonus x 2 percent.
Chance for another magic weapon to be sentient is highest magical bonus percent.
Double that chance for Life Drinker, Luck Blade, Vorpal Blade, and Dwarven Thrower.

generation.step: Determine whether the weapon is sentient.
If sentient, determine Intelligence, Alignment, Ego, Willpower, and Powers.

sentient_weapons.rule: Empathy conveys intuitive knowledge of powers and use without words.
Read Languages is always active and functions as the arcane spell.
In addition to maker language, weapon knows extra languages from a 1d20 roll: 01-10 one, 11-14 two, 15-17 three, 18 four, 19 five, 20 six.

alignment_rules.rule: A character may only wield a sentient sword with the same alignment.
Touching or wielding a sword of differing alignment causes 1d6 damage per degree of alignment difference each round.

ego_and_willpower.rule: Weapon base willpower = INT + EGO + 1 per spell-like power.
Character willpower = WIS + STR + 1 per level beyond 8.
If wounded but at 50% hp or more, subtract 1d4 from character willpower.
If below 50% hp, subtract 2d4 from character willpower.
Weapon gets +1d10 willpower if its alignment differs from the character's.
Influence checks occur when first touched, when motivation is relevant, when touched by different alignment, when another magic sword is found, and when a character has lost 50% of hp.
Higher willpower wins the influence check.
If the character loses, the Judge determines a period of control during which the weapon forces action serving its desires.

motivations.rule: 5% chance to have a special motivation; roll 01-05 on d00.
If motivated, set INT and EGO both to 12.

Against a motivated target, chaotic weapons energy drain 1 level per magical bonus, lawful weapons deal 1 extra damage die per magical bonus, and neutral weapons grant the wielder an AC and saving throw bonus equal to the weapon's magical bonus.

powers.rule: Sentient weapons have detection powers and spell-like powers.
The wielder must hold the weapon to activate or maintain a power.
No more than one power can be active at once.
Each detection power can be used up to 3 times per day.
All spell-like powers together can be used 3 times total per day.
When rolling for powers, reroll or ignore identical results where required.

selling.rule: Adventurers sell self-made items for twice the base cost to create them.
Adventurers sell identified found items for the base cost to create them.
A market must be large enough to have buyers.
Chance or quantity of buyers per month depends on item price and market class.

buying.rule: Adventurers buy magic items for twice the base cost to create them.
A market must be large enough to have sellers.
Availability per month depends on item price and market class.
Even large markets usually have only small quantities available.

commissioning.rule: Commissioned magic-item creators for hire are found only in Class I markets or through adventuring contacts.
The commissioner pays the item's base cost, precious materials, and any required special components up front.
On successful completion, the commissioner pays an additional fee equal to 7,000 gp per month or twice the base cost, whichever is greater.
Base creation cost and time come from the Magic Item Creation rules in the magic research chapter.
